title: Why Diamonds Cost More Than Water (Even Though Water Keeps You Alive)
description:
Water is essential and diamonds aren't, so why does water cost almost nothing? A 200-year-old economics puzzle explains it.

Educational content, not financial advice.

#shorts #financefacts #economics

scenes.text: You need water to survive. You do not need diamonds. So why is water nearly free, and diamonds are not?
Economists call this the diamond water paradox, and it puzzled thinkers for over a century.
The answer isn't about how useful something is overall. It's about how much one more unit of it is worth to you, right now.
Water is everywhere, so one more glass barely matters. Diamonds are scarce, so one more diamond matters a lot to whoever wants it.
Economists call this idea marginal value, and it's the foundation of how modern pricing actually works.
Scarcity, not importance, is usually what sets the price. That single idea reshaped economics.
